scope: For a JHT member whose employer is not a state organ, 5.7 percent of wages must go in each month: 2 percent from the worker and 3.7 percent from the employer (Pemerintah Republik Indonesia, 2015b).

[data/README.md] It also checks coverage: a single credited rate for each year of the window, no credited rate after it, no second yield in any year, and exactly the bonus rows `R3` lists. `test_extract_jht.py` corrupts the manifest in the ways those checks are meant to catch and confirms each corruption stops the script. - **What the manifest's notes record.** Where each rate comes from: the notes to the financial statements for the earlier years with an annual decree, and for 2016 to 2020 the reports' narrative sections, as design amendment `A1` records.

[data/README.md] Design amendment `A1` keeps the IMF index for `R5` and `R6`; the year-by-year chart also shows, in some years, JHT's rate against BPS's published December rate. - **United States.** Fetched for this post from the IMF's SDMX API in the same format.

findings.claim: For a JHT member whose employer is not a state organ, 5.7 percent of wages must go in each month: 2 percent from the worker and 3.7 percent from the employer (Pemerintah Republik Indonesia, 2015b).
findings.evidence:
S: I read sources/text/pp_46_2015.txt. Pasal 16(1) (lines 426-436) reads: 'Iuran JHT bagi Peserta penerima Upah yang bekerja pada Pemberi Kerja selain penyelenggara negara sebesar 5,7% ... dari Upah', with 2% 'ditanggung oleh Pekerja' and 3,7% 'ditanggung oleh Pemberi Kerja'. 'JHT member' is a faithful rendering of Peserta: Pasal 1 angka 3 (line 67) defines 'Peserta JHT yang selanjutnya disebut Peserta'. 'Employer is not a state organ' renders 'Pemberi Kerja selain penyelenggara negara' (Pasal 1 angka 2, line 61, 'penyelenggara negara yang memperkerjakan pegawai negeri'; Pasal 3, line 131, sends state employers to a separate regulation; Pasal 4(1)a, line 140). The draft does not render Pasal 16's 'penerima Upah' (wage-earning), but the gap is closed by 'whose employer' together with 'of wages'. The non-wage members in Pasal 4(3) (lines 152-157: employers themselves, the self-employed, other workers who are not paid wages) have no wages for a percentage to apply to, and Pasal 18 sets their contribution as nominal amounts instead. 'Each month' is supported: Pasal 17(1) (line 444) sets the base as 'Upah sebulan', and Pasal 19(2) (line 511) says 'Pemberi Kerja wajib membayar Iuran ... setiap bulan paling lambat tanggal 15'. 'Must go in' is supported: Pasal 19(1) (line 507) says 'Pemberi Kerja selain penyelenggara negara wajib menyetor Iuran JHT ... sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 16'. No later regulation changes the rate. pp_60_2015_kemnaker.txt:70 amends only Pasal 26, and permenaker_4_2022 concerns benefits. The citation 2015b is PP 46/2015 (draft .md:137), and its URL equals sources.json pp46_jht_contribution.fetched_from. Two notes, neither an error. Pasal 17(2) narrows the wage base to basic wage plus fixed allowances; 'of wages' follows Pasal 16's 'dari Upah'. And 'state organ' is a gloss; 'state administrator' would be closer to 'penyelenggara negara'. | L: The figures and the scope match the bound key. sources/text/pp_46_2015.txt (sha 8345590b, matches sources.json) :428-434, Pasal 16(1): 'Iuran JHT bagi Peserta penerima Upah yang bekerja pada Pemberi Kerja selain penyelenggara negara sebesar 5,7% ... 2% ... Pekerja ... 3,7% ... Pemberi Kerja'. 'Must' is Pasal 19(1), 'wajib menyetor Iuran JHT ... sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 16' (:505-509). 'Each month' is Pasal 19(2), 'setiap bulan' (:510-512), and Pasal 17(1), 'Upah sebulan' (:442-446). The locator of sources.json pp46_jht_contribution is 'JHT contribution for wage earners whose employer is not a state organ', the same wording as the sentence. Universal: the sentence is conditional on being a JHT member. It no longer says membership is compulsory, which was the r1:item:18 defect (phasing in Pasal 2(1) :116-121; the IR 2024 coverage gap). The narrowness does not mislead. Pasal 3 (:131-134) sends JHT for participants at state employers to a separate PP, so implying that other JHT members exist is accurate. 'Not a state organ' still covers SOEs, as round 1's skeptic required. Antecedent: 'JHT member' names JHT, so 'A separate pension scheme' has something to be separate from. The paragraph argues validly: rate, then JP excluded with its reason. The MDX at :22 is identical. Style note: 'must go in' lost its explicit object 'into JHT' (round 2's L2 fix), so only 'JHT member' carries the destination. A reader still gets JHT from it and from the 'separate' contrast that follows, so this is not refuted. | H: Draft .md:13, .src.md:13 and site MDX:22 all carry the identical new sentence. The snapshot diff (.rounds/3.json to 4.json) shows the only change: 'Each month 5.7 percent of wages must go into JHT' became 'For a JHT member whose employer is not a state organ, 5.7 percent of wages must go in each month'. The rate and its scope match PP 46/2015 Pasal 16(1) (sources/text/pp_46_2015.txt:428-434), which reads 'Iuran JHT bagi Peserta penerima Upah yang bekerja pada Pemberi Kerja selain penyelenggara negara sebesar 5,7% ... 2% ... Pekerja ... 3,7% ... Pemberi Kerja'. 'Must' and 'each month' rest on Pasal 19(1)-(2) (txt:507-513: 'wajib menyetor ... setiap bulan').

The hostile-reader tests:
(a) Clarity to an Indonesian reader. Pasal 1 angka 2 (txt:57-63) defines the state-side employer as 'penyelenggara negara yang memperkerjakan pegawai negeri', a state body that employs civil servants. 'Not a state organ' therefore reads as 'not a government employer', which is the right category. The English term does not exclude workers at state-owned enterprises (BUMN), which are companies.
(b) The qualifier is not vacuous. Pasal 3 (txt:131-134) sends JHT at state employers to a separate PP, so the regulation itself expects members at state employers.
(c) 'JHT member whose employer' excludes non-wage members. Pasal 4(1) (txt:140-151) limits wage-earning members to non-state employers. Non-wage members (BPU) have no employer and pay a fixed amount under Pasal 18 (txt:477-482), not 5.7 percent.
(d) Scoping to 'JHT member' avoids the coverage universal that round 3 refuted. IR 2024 (bpjs_ir_2024.txt:8433-8437) counts 29,308,491 wage-earner (PU) members in JKK/JKM but only 18,425,867 PU in JHT.
(e) A BPJS official's own material agrees. BPJS's JHT simulator page (sources/text/bpjs_tetap_sejahtera.txt:52, fetched 2026-10-21) says 'Iuran perusahaan 3,7%, Iuran TK 2%'. I found nothing in the stored sources that contradicts the sentence.

Notes (style, not refuted):
- The fix replaced 'must go into JHT' with 'must go in'. The destination round 2 (r2:extra:L2) added is now only implied through 'JHT member'. Optional narrowing to the bound key's 'Iuran JHT': '... must go into JHT each month'.
- 'State organ' is the bound key's own term (sources.json pp46_jht_contribution locator). A lay rendering such as 'not the government' would be friendlier to read, but that is a style choice.
- The locator's 'wage earners' is dropped, but 'whose employer' implies it.
- 'Wages' simplifies Pasal 17(2)'s base, 'Upah pokok dan tunjangan tetap'. This was not changed in round 3

findings.evidence: Quoted sentence (draft .md:13, src:13, MDX:22): 'A separate pension scheme, Jaminan Pensiun, takes another 3 percent (Pemerintah Republik Indonesia, 2015a); it pays a pension, so I leave it out of the growth comparison.' Round 3 rewrote the sentence before it into an explicit member-level frame: 'For a JHT member whose employer is not a state organ, 5.7 percent of wages must go in each month'. Inside that frame, 'another 3 percent' says that every such JHT member also pays JP. That is the r1:item:18 class of compulsory-coverage universal again, this time for JP. Three stored sources contradict it. (1) PP 45 Pasal 4(1) (pp_45_2015.txt:184-187) phases JP registration in: 'sesuai penahapan kepesertaan'. (2) BPJS IR 2024 (sources/text/bpjs_ir_2024.txt:8436 and :8448) counts 18,425,867 active wage-earner (PU) JHT members against 14,959,033 JP members, 'seluruhnya merupakan PU'. So at least 3,466,834 (18.8%) of the JHT members the frame describes pay no JP (computed: 18,425,867 - 14,959,033). Under PP 46 Pasal 4(1)(a), JHT PU members are all at non-state employers. (3) Pasal 29(2) (:855-858) caps the JP wage base; r2:item:2 accepted that point as following the regulation's own wording, and I do not re-raise it. Not new in round 3: round 1's S lens noted 'not every JHT payer pays JP' (r1:item:20), but no fix took it up. Round 3's explicit member scope now binds 'another' to that member. The paragraph otherwise argues validly, and 'separate' has its antecedent (JHT). | skeptic: Quote confirmed at draft .md:13, .src.md:13 (bound key pp45_jp_total) and site MDX :22. Round 3's member frame ('For a JHT member whose employer is not a state organ, 5.7 percent ... must go in') sits right before it, so 'another 3 percent' reads as more money taken from that same member's wages. That is false for a sizeable minority of those members. (1) PP 45 Pasal 4(1) (pp_45_2015.txt:184-188) makes JP registration a duty only 'sesuai penahapan kepesertaan' (phased). (2) bpjs_ir_2024.txt:8436-8437 gives 18,425,867 active JHT wage-earner (PU) members, and :8448-8449 gives 14,959,033 JP members, 'seluruhnya merupakan PU'. I computed 18,425,867 - 14,959,033 = 3,466,834, which is 18.82% (saved at skeptic-L/jp_gap.txt). This lower bound holds without assuming JP members are a subset of JHT members, because |A minus B| >= |A| - |B|. (3) PP 46 Pasal 4(1)(a) (pp_46_2015.txt:139-141) puts every JHT PU member at a non-state employer, so they all fall inside the sentence's frame. The 3 percent rate itself is correct (pp_45_2015.txt:820-822, Pasal 28(2)). Only the per-member scope is wrong. Round 1's S lens recorded 'not every JHT payer pays JP' (p28r1/run1.json results/0/verdicts/1). Its fix only deleted 'rather than building a balance' (p28r2/round1_fixes.txt:10). Round 2 kept the 3 percent on the wage-ceiling point alone (p28r2/run2.json results/0/verdicts/0), so this point was never resolved. Severity LOW is right: the paragraph's reasoning and its 'separate' antecedent are sound.

findings.evidence:
Context touched by round 3. The sentence is draft .md:13, .src.md:13 and MDX:22: 'A separate pension scheme, Jaminan Pensiun, takes another 3 percent (Pemerintah Republik Indonesia, 2015a); it pays a pension, so I leave it out of the growth comparison.'

Round 3 scoped the sentence before it to 'a JHT member whose employer is not a state organ'. 'Another' now ties JP's 3 percent to that same member. That is not true of every such member:
- Active members: IR 2024 (sources/text/bpjs_ir_2024.txt:8435-8449) counts 18,425,867 wage-earner (PU) members in JHT and 14,959,033 in JP, 'seluruhnya merupakan PU'. So at least 18,425,867 - 14,959,033 = 3,466,834 active wage-earner JHT members (about 19 percent) pay nothing to JP. This is the same coverage standard round 3 used to refute item 1.
- Pay above the cap: PP 45/2015 Pasal 29(2) (pp_45_2015.txt:855-858) caps the wage base, so for pay above the ceiling JP takes less than 3 percent.

This is not a regression. Before round 3 the paragraph was fully unscoped, so round 3 narrowed the implied population. Round 1's S lens raised the JHT-vs-JP membership gap (r1:item:20), and the fix did not address it. Round 2 confirmed the sentence and noted the cap. The rate itself is right: Pasal 28(2), '3% (tiga persen) dari Upah per bulan', which is the bound key pp45_jp_total. An Indonesian worker at a small firm enrolled in JHT but not JP would read the paragraph as saying 3 percent should also go to JP. | skeptic: The finding stands at LOW. I re-checked each part myself. (1) The sentence is identical in draft .md:13, in .src.md:13 (where it is bound to {{src:pp45_jp_total.values.total_pct:int}}) and in site MDX src/content/blog/forced-to-save-and-i-never-knew-it.mdx:22. It comes right after round 3's scoped sentence, 'For a JHT member whose employer is not a state organ, 5.7 percent ...', so 'another' adds JP's 3 percent for that same member. (2) The rate is right. sources/text/pp_45_2015.txt (sha256 995c021e..., which matches sources.json pp45_jp_total) has Pasal 28(2) at lines 822-823: 'sebesar 3% (tiga persen) dari Upah per bulan'. (3) The population is wrong, both in law and in practice. In law, Pasal 4(1) (pp_45_2015.txt:184-188) requires employers to register workers only 'sesuai penahapan kepesertaan berdasarkan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan', so JP is phased in by separate regulation and is not owed for every JHT member at a non-state employer. In practice, sources/text/bpjs_ir_2024.txt:8435-8449 counts 18,425,867 PU (wage-earner) members in JHT and 14,959,033 in JP, 'seluruhnya merupakan PU'. That gives 18,425,867 - 14,959,033 = 3,466,834 (18.8 percent, computed) as a lower bound on active wage-earner JHT members outside JP. The bound holds even without assuming every JP member is also in JHT. (4) The cap is also right: Pasal 29(2) at :855-858 limits the JP wage base (Rp7,000,000 in 2015, indexed), so above the cap JP takes less than 3 percent of pay. Round 2 accepted this as following the regulation's own '3% dari Upah'. (5) The history checks out. Round 1's S verdict on item 20 (p28r1/run1.json) cited the same 14,959,033 vs 18,425,867 gap, but its fix deleted only 'rather than building a balance'. Round 2 (p28r2/run2.json, S id 2) confirmed the sentence and noted the cap. Round 3 refuted item 1 using IR 2024 counts and 'penahapan kepesertaan', so the finding's appeal to 'the same coverage standard' is accurate. This is a gap that predates round 3, not a regression, so LOW is right. One problem with the finding's proposed fix: in this paragraph 'from X' names who pays ('2 percent from the worker and 3.7 percent from the employer'). So '3 percent from its members' would say members pay all 3 percent. That contradicts Pasal 28(3) (pp_45_2015.txt:824-831; bound key pp45_jp_split), under which the employer pays 2 percent and the worker 1 percent.
